text: The question (Kourovka notebook, Problem 20.84). Let Δ be the augmentation ideal of Z[G], Dn(G)=G∩(1+Δn) the dimension subgroups and γn(G) the lower central series. Always γn⊆ Dn, and Dn=γn for n≤3; for n=4 this fails (Rips). Is D5(G)⊆γ4(G) for every group?

For Lie rings the answer is yes (Ionin, Mikhailov, Petrov, 2026, formalized in Lean). For groups it is open, and we have not solved it. This site shows what is proved, what is computed, and what is left.
True for every finite group whose Sylow 2-subgroup has order ≤210, in particular for all groups of order <2048.
Order 211: ranks 2–4 and ≥8 closed, 5–7 open.
No 3-torsion in D5/γ5 when the Sylow 3-subgroup has order ≤39.
On paper for all groups whose G/γ2 has at most one invariant larger than 3 (e.g. exponent 3, or C9× C3s-1), of any order.
D5(L)⊆γ4(L) for Lie rings; the formalization audited. The group question and the reduction to 2-groups of class 3 are stated in Lean.
No computed group has D5≠γ5; in all of them Dn=γn for every n. Over a hundred thousand candidates, all computations exact.
A cell stands for all 2-groups of class 3 of the given order and rank; it is closed when all of them have D5=1. 33 cells are closed and 3 open. More on the coverage map page.
C computer C+P computer + paper P paper ? open. Empty cells: no such groups.
On paper: D5=γ5 when Q/γ2 has at most one invariant larger than 3 (including C9× C3s-1); an independent review found no errors.
References: what Tahara actually announced (p. 173), and the search for his separate paper.
Computer check for C9× C3s-1 and C27,C81× C3s-1: 2 057 groups, 4 537 elements z, none in D5.
ANUPQ audit (ispacex.github.io/gap): the 39 descendant step was repeated with the fixed version, and the result is byte-identical.
On paper: Dn(H E)=Dn(H) for central products with D8, Q8 and M2k+2 (adjoining a central square root); all 386 candidates of orders 26–29 satisfy the conditions. Two independent reviews.

On paper: gluing along a proper subgroup of Z(E) — a lemma on central roots of any degree (Lemma 5.9). The splittings of the 386 candidates: 20 split, each has a splitting covered by Prop. 5.8. An independent review and a recount by another method.
Lean: Lemma 5.9 (a central root of any degree) is proved in Lean, with no sorry and only the standard axioms; formalizing the other paper results has started.
Lean: Prop. 5.8 is proved in Lean in all cases (D8, Q8, M2k+2), with the ring statement Z[H]∩Δ(Q)n=Δ(H)n; Q8 and M2k+2 reduce to D8 through one overgroup (Q×Z)/(s,-2).

Lean: the reduction (Prop. 2.1, Remark 2.3) is proved modulo explicit hypotheses — the theorems of Passi and Gruenberg and D3=γ3: from class ≤3 to finitely generated groups and to finite 2-groups of class 3; for finite groups Gruenberg's theorem is not needed.

Lean: Lemma 6.3 and Prop. 6.5 ([γ2,γ2]⊆γ5; a non-metabelian p-group of class 4 and rank d has order ≥ pd+5) are proved in Lean with no hypotheses; instead of the Lie ring, the group G/γ5 and the Hall–Witt identity.
